concepts.title: The Farmer's Knowledge
concepts.definition: Indian farming rests on knowledge handed down for millennia; the Krishi Parashara verse quoted in the chapter praises the farmer who knows his cattle, his seasons and his seeds, and is rewarded with harvests of every kind.
concepts.key_idea: Farming is a science of observation: seasons, seeds and soil read carefully, season after season.

concepts.title: How Farming Began
concepts.definition: Farming began when communities learnt to save seeds and settle near fields: wild grasses were tamed into crops, forests cleared, and wandering food-gatherers slowly became villagers tied to the rhythm of sowing and harvest.
concepts.key_idea: The seed saved today is the field of tomorrow: settling down to grow food changed society forever.

concepts.title: Crops of India
concepts.definition: Indian fields grow a rich variety: rice in the monsoon wet, wheat and mustard in the winter cool, millets on dry land, besides cotton, sugarcane, tea and spices, each crop matched to its season and region.
concepts.key_idea: Crop follows climate: the same subcontinent grows rice in one state and wheat in another.

concepts.title: Water for the Fields
concepts.definition: Rain alone cannot feed the fields, so farmers built wells, tanks, canals and check dams from ancient times; irrigation lets a second crop grow and shields the harvest when the monsoon fails.
concepts.key_idea: Water is farming's first input: whoever stores and shares it wisely doubles the land's gift.
